catalog_locator: §3.3 Tones, p. 4; §1 Introduction, p. 2; §3 Phonology header, p. 3
catalog_quote: 3.3 Tones The tone system of Bu has three level tones. No cases of glide tones seem to occur. [§1, p. 2] The wordlist was collected as a ‘one-shot’ exercise and the transcription must therefore be regarded as very preliminary. In general, tones are not marked, although the data was taped and they will be added when time permits. [§3, p. 3] The phonology of Bu is based on rapid observations and should therefore be regarded as tentative at this stage.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (20 pp., PDF metadata 'Bu wordlist Unicode.doc', created 19 Oct 2011) and its text. The quoted passage is there exactly: '3.3 Tones / The tone system of Bu has three level tones. No cases of glide tones seem to occur.' on printed p. 4 = PDF page 5 of 20 (extracted text), not p. 6 as the report said; the p. 2 sentence 'In general, tones are not marked, although the data was taped and they will be added when time permits.' is also verbatim. I read the whole document: §3 Phonology (printed pp. 3-4) is explicitly 'based on rapid observations and should therefore be regarded as tentative'; it gives a 7-vowel + 3-nasal-vowel chart, a consonant chart and the two-sentence tone note; §4 morph…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only phonological description on record treats Bu as a three-level-tone language (H, M, L; no contour tones) and says nothing about word stress or accent; no stress placement rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author notes the /ə/ status is uncertain and that the phonology 'is based on rapid observations and should therefore be regarded as tentative' (p. 3).
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation-form wordlist elicited in one session (Nakere village, 8 Jan 1999); tones unmarked in the list; author calls the phonology 'tentative'. No statement about word-level prominence, stress or accent at all.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog buuu1244 'Bu' = the Bu (Abu) half of Blench's Bu-Ningkada cluster (Atlas ed. 3 entry 54: 54.a Bu, 54.b Ningkada; dialects Jida, Abu, Raga). Blench 2011's data are from the Bu (Abu) variety at Nakere village; the Ningkada (Jidda) variety, which Blench considers the same language with minor lexical/phonological differences, is not described separately. Not to be confused with the Chadic 'Bu (Zaranda)' [zbu] created in the same ISO 2020-031 cycle.

The 'current revision' hoped for in the citation does not exist: two direct downloads of the rogerblench.info URL returned an HTTP 202 captcha redirect, but the the Internet Archive's index index (queried) lists eight captures of that URL from 2015-04-21 to 2025-05-28, all with digest HOMTKL5F4JNLQJYRU2SZO3YWTZNHLWFI, which I verified equals the SHA-1/base32 of the on-disk 2015 capture; so the file on the site is byte-identical to the 19 Oct 2011 printout and no tone-marked revision has been posted. Two downloads of the 2025-05-28 capture itself failed (web.archive.org refused connections on 443 and 80 by automat…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bu is described as a tone language with three level tones and no contour (glide) tones; the document says nothing about stress, accent or prominence anywhere (the words 'stress', 'accent' and 'prominence' do not occur). The wordlist itself is untoned except for two stray forms (no. 12 ikə́la 'charcoal II', no. 470 éyivi).
new_statements.exceptions: none; the author flags the transcription as very preliminary and the tone marking as not yet done
new_statements.identity_note: Blench's data are Bu proper, elicited at Nakere village (Plateau State) on 8 Jan 1999 from Joshua Chaga and elders, with additional 1980 data from Muzha Bana in Kafanchan. Blench 1999 (Ogmios 11, held by the project) treats Bu and Ningkada/Jidda as the same language 'with some minor lexical and phonological differences'; ISO jid covers the Bu-Ningkada cluster, Glottolog buuu1244 = Bu. No dialect-specific tone or stress claims are made.
